<a id="context"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/md/brand-guidelines-02.svg" alt="Context: What: Netra grades the carbon credits a company says it retired. Registry data, published research, the company&#x27;s own report and an independent emissions estimate, side by side. Each check is recorded on a public blockchain. For: the public and journalists (is this claim real?), scientists (open data and method), buyers and auditors (due diligence), regulators (EU Directive 2024/825 on green claims). Name: netra is Sanskrit for &quot;eye&quot;, also known in Indonesian. Short, easy to say worldwide." width="100%"></p>

<a id="positioning"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/md/brand-guidelines-03.svg" alt="Positioning: Sylvera, BeZero and Calyx grade carbon projects, behind paywalls. CarbonPlan publishes open research but does not grade companies. Climate TRACE estimates emissions only. Netra grades the claim a company makes, free, with every source linked and every check on the record. Proof points: 876 Mt retired since 2020, searchable by buyer; 44,465 buyers; primary-source emissions for 79 of 94 classified company groups (94.3% of company tonnes)." width="100%"></p>

<a id="identity"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/md/brand-guidelines-04.svg" alt="Identity: Mark: an eye whose iris is half filled with the signal colour: the share of a claim that holds up. Always with the lowercase wordmark netra (Hanken Grotesk 600, tracking −0.04em). Mark alone for favicon and app icon. Colour: ink #121212, paper #FBFAF7, one signal #E8590C, line #E6E2DA. No green (the colour of greenwashing). Dark sections are reserved for proof (on-chain record). Grades: A #1D4E89, B #3A6FB0, C #D9D4CB, D #F2A36B, E #B83A0E. Blue to orange, readable with colour blindness; the letter is always printed on the swatch. Type: Hanken Grotesk for everything (headlines 600, b" width="100%"></p>

<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/palette.svg" alt="Colour and type" width="100%"></p>

<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/grades.svg" alt="Grade scale" width="100%"></p>

<a id="voice"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/md/brand-guidelines-05.svg" alt="Voice: Blunt, factual, calm. Short sentences. Every claim carries a number and a source. No outrage words (&quot;scam&quot;, &quot;fraud&quot;, &quot;shocking&quot;). The data does the talking. We write: &quot;Shell retired 42.3 Mt of credits since 2020. Research covers 23.3 Mt of them. About 5.3 Mt are likely real. Range: 0.3 to 19.9 Mt. Sources below.&quot; We never write: &quot;Shell&#x27;s shocking offset scam exposed!&quot; The method line is stated as fact, not apology: &quot;Estimates from published research (Probst et al. 2024) applied to registry data. Every number links to its source. Check them.&quot;" width="100%"></p>

<a id="messaging"></a>
<p align="center"><img src="../docs/assets/md/brand-guidelines-06.svg" alt="Messaging: Tagline: See what a carbon claim is really worth. Value line: Type a company. See the credits it retired, how many research says are likely real, what it reports emitting, and what independent estimates see. Headline facts: about 1 in 5 researched tonnes likely real (19.4%, range 2.4–68.8%, flat since 2020); 57% of tonnes cannot be tied to a named claimant (41% blank); none of the 52 gradable large buyers reaches a B; 4.5% carry the ICVCM quality label; for 4 of 14 comparable groups the independent estimate is 3–6× reported Scope 1. Proof line: Every published check is on the record" width="100%"></p>
